title: Understanding Logistic Regression
text: In logistic regression, the probability $$\$P(Y=1|X)\$$$ is modeled using the logistic function, which outputs values between $$0$$ and $$1$$. This means that $$\$P(Y=1|X)\$$$ can never be exactly $$1$$ or $$0$$, but it can get very close to these values. Think about how this affects the statement $P(Y=1|X)<1$.

title: Behavior of the Logistic Function
text: The logistic function $\sigma(z)=1/(1+e**{-z})$ is always less than $$1$$ because the denominator $1+e**{-z}$ is always greater than $$1$$. How does this relate to the probability $$\$P(Y=1|X)\$$$?
